we propose an algorithm for learning policies in parallel differentiable simulators that is able to leverage simulation gradients even when simulators are non-smooth, and that this algorithm can be applied to challenging control tasks, achieving substantial improvements in sample and wall-clock time efficiency.

we propose a high-performance differentiatoriable simulator and learning algorithm that can be effectively applied to complex control tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of sample efficiency and wall clock time.

1) we present an algorithm that combines differentiable simulation with a truncated learning window to achieve a $>17\times$ increase in sample efficiency for a challenging locomotion task; 2) we show that the same approach can be applied to other control tasks and achieves comparable results to state-of-the-art methods; and 3) we demonstrate that our approach can be used to learn complex policies in high-dimensional spaces with large action spaces.

differentiable simulation can be used to learn control policies in complex environments with a large number of states and actions.
